subject: Re: FinBank - eval setup & next steps (model recommendations + dataset format)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia@finbank.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinBank - eval setup & next steps (model recommendations + dataset format)

Hi Sofia — great call today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment: 

Recap:
- Use case: customer support triage + suggested responses (sensitive PII redaction required).
- Success criteria: intent classification accuracy >= 92% on holdout, response-to-agent pass rate >= 88% (human-eval).
- Constraints: data cannot leave FinBank VPC for Private offering; for initial eval we can run in Redwood Dedicated in us-east with encrypted volumes.

Recommended first-pass models to evaluate (fast/cheap -> high quality):
1) redwood-2x-16k (fp16) — good latency/quality balance for short replies.
2) llama-3-70b-q4f16 (quantized) — stronger quality for complex rewrites; expect higher token cost.
3) redwood-1-8k-quant (8-bit) — cost-optimized baseline for throughput tests.

Benchmarks & prompt sets:
- Attached: redwood-benchmarks-q2-2027.pdf (shows previous finserv benchmarks).
- Attached: finbank_eval_promptset_v1.csv — canonical prompts + expected label schema.
- Also linking our eval runner: https://app.redwood.com/console/evals/FB-2027-09

Dataset/format we need for running customer-specific evals on Redwood:
- Preferred: JSONL (newline-delimited). Each record: id, input, expected_output, metadata. Example: {\"id\": \"case_0001\", \"input\": \"Customer: my card was charged twice...\", \"expected_output\": \"Apologize, confirm transaction ids, and initiate refund if duplicate\" }
- For classification tasks include a "labels" array and gold_label field.
- Max dataset size to start: 1k-5k examples; we can scale after first pass.

Scoring criteria we propose:
- Exact match / intent accuracy for classification tasks.
- ROUGE-L / semantic similarity + human pass-fail for response quality.
- Regression detection: baseline thresholds and automatic alerts if model quality drops >3% v baseline.

Next steps (action items):
1) Sofia to share a 500-1,000 sample extract (de-identified) in the JSONL template by Wed 30 Jun.
2) Redwood (Dev) to provision a sandbox eval runner and load the dataset; expected ETA 48 hours after receipt.
3) Marissa/Neha to run recommended model sweep and deliver initial results + recommended config (batching/quant) within 5 business days.

If helpful I can drop in a short note describing the JSONL template; attaching redwood_eval_template.jsonl as a starter.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

—
Marissa Cole

Thanks Sofia — noted. Quick follow-up on two items: 

1) Cost estimate (rough) for 1k-sample full eval sweep (in USD):
   - redwood-1-8k-quant (baseline): ~$120- $180 (compute + token charges)
   - redwood-2x-16k: ~$220- $320
   - llama-3-70b-q4f16: ~$450- $700
   These are ballpark; final depends on avg token length and whether we enable caching/batching.

2) JSONL template details (attached redwood_eval_template.jsonl). Minimal required fields: id, input, expected_output, task_type (classification/generation), gold_label(s). Metadata (optional): customer_id, channel, timestamp.

Dev — can you confirm ETA to provision a dedicated sandbox eval runner in us-east and an initial job to process a 1k JSONL? Let's assume data will be de-identified.

Marissa

On it — I spun up a Dedicated sandbox cluster (us-east-1) and pre-seeded the eval runner with the redwood_eval_template.jsonl. ETA: I can ingest the 1k sample and run the three-model sweep within 36 hours of receiving the dataset.

Notes for Marissa/Neha:
- Please ask Sofia to keep avg input length under ~800 tokens for the initial run (helps cost predictability).
- We'll enable KV-prefix caching and a small batch window to optimize throughput; I will record per-token cost and latency per model and upload results to the console link.

I attached a short stub script in the console under the eval job (link included in related_links) that automates scoring (accuracy + rouge) and triggers regression alerts if delta >3%.
